In order to facilitate public participation at meetings held solely by
electronic means, the City will accept public comment in the following manner:
1. During the meeting, members of the public may provide live public comment by
submitting a speaker card prior to the start of public comment on that item, at
the following webpage:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment

indicate so on the online form (multiple item speakers will be handled according
to the process posted on the agenda and as specified in the City Council meeting
policy). Public comments are limited to 3 minutes each, and the Mayor and City
Council may limit this time if reasonable under the circumstances.

virtual meeting in order to locate and unmute the speaker.

Council Minutes  1  04/1 9/2021
   Mayor Gordo announced a proclamation declaring April 24, 2021
  as "Day of Remembrance of the Armenian Genocide" in Pasadena,
  which will be presented to Shoghig Yepremian, Chair of the
  Armenian National Committee of America, Pasadena Chapter.

-  Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the City's actions to
  acknowledge the Armenian genocide, including the Armenian
  Genocide Memorial located in Old Pasadena's Memorial Park. He
  acknowledge the death of Mr. Donnell Williams (father of City
  employee Dennis Williams), and expressed condolences to the
  family.

  PUBLIC COMMENT  The following individuals expressed concerns with the Pasadena
  Police Department and officers; in support of an Independent
  Police Auditor, and spoke on the need for alternatives to policing
  measures in the City, including certain social services:

  Jane Ward, Altadena resident
  Mx Kat Ross, Altadena resident
  Stephanie Blank, Altadena resident

  Steve Mermell, City Manager, provided information on the
  recommended Capital Improvement Program Budget that was
  presented to the Planning Commission; and responded to
  questions.

  Councilmember Kennedy requested that staff provide additional
  information on the Police Departments' Capital Improvement
  Program project funds of $5,000,000 to enhance and update the
  Pasadena Police Department building at a future Finance
  Committee meeting.

  The following individuals advocated for the City Council to rezone
  land owned by churches and other religious organizations to allow
  for building and providing affordable housing:

  Bert Newton, Pasadena resident
  Philip Burns, Pasadena resident

  Councilmember Kennedy asked Mayor Gordo, the Housing
  Taskforce, and staff move forward as soon as possible with the
  discussion on congregational land overlay zoning as the City is in
  need of affordable housing units.

  In response to Mayor Gordo's inquiry related to the City's Draft
  Housing Element report, City Manager Mermell responded that
  staff believes the report will be ready by May of 2021

Council Minutes  4  04/19/2021
   City Manager Mermell responded that staff is prepared to follow the
  instructions directed by the City Council, and provided information
  on the City's current cannabis regulations related to possible
  cannabis operators; and responded to questions.

  David Reyes, Director of Planning and Community Development,
  provided information on the City's Zoning Code related to the
  cannabis permit deadline, applications, and application process;
  and responded to questions.

  Vice Mayor Wilson spoke in favor of postponing the Public Hearing
  until the April 26, 2021, City Council meeting.

  Mayor Gordo expressed concerns with rushing the proposed

  "Alluding to an organization called POP!, which is a more loosely, I
